title: Degree and dimension bounds for sub-linear series on a smooth curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective], and put $g=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\geq2$ [def-pc-genus]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] of degree $d$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], and let $0\ne U\subset H^0(C,L)$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace of dimension $q$. The image $A_U=\operatorname{im}(U\otimes_k\mathcal O_C\longrightarrow L)$ of evaluation is an invertible submodule of $L$, generated by $U$. Its degree $a=\deg A_U$ satisfies $0\leq a\leq d$, and
$$q\leq h^0(C,A_U)\leq\max\{a+1-g,\ a/2+1\}.$$
Here $h^0$ denotes the dimension of global sections and the maximum is taken in $\mathbf R$. If $q=1$, then $A_U\simeq\mathcal O_C$ and $a=0$. If $U=H^0(C,L)$ and evaluation is surjective, then $A_U=L$ and $a=d$. Scheme conventions are [def-pc-scheme].

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $C$ is proper. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], $C$ is Noetherian and integral, with generic point $\eta$, function field $K=k(C)$, and DVR local rings at its closed points; all other points equal $\eta$. Choose a basis $s_1,\ldots,s_q$ of $U$. By [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] each $s_i$ has nonzero generic germ. Its divisor $D_i=\operatorname{div}_L(s_i)$ is defined and finitely supported by [def-sc-rational-section-divisor]. Each coefficient is nonnegative: in a local generator of $L$ the coefficient of a global section belongs to the local DVR. Set $b_P=\min_i\operatorname{ord}_P(s_i)$ and $B=\sum_P b_P[P]$. Since $0\leq b_P\leq\operatorname{ord}_P(s_1)$, this is a finite effective divisor.

source.place: Tags 02SF (definition-order-vanishing-meromorphic), 0BE6 (definition-divisor-invertible-sheaf), 01X5 (lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme); minimum orders of a finite basis

proof.text: At a closed point $P$, trivialize $L_P$ and choose a uniformizer $t$. If $s_i=f_i e$, the image of evaluation is the ideal $(f_1,\ldots,f_q)e=t^{b_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}e$: an $f_i$ with minimal order is $t^{b_P}$ times a unit and every other $f_j$ is divisible by $t^{b_P}$. By [lem-sc-divisor-module-local], $\mathcal O_C(-B)_P=t^{b_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$ and $\mathcal O_C(-B)$ is invertible. Thus the natural submodule $L\otimes\mathcal O_C(-B)\subseteq L$ has the same stalks as $A_U$ at all closed points, At $\eta$, the nonzero germ of $s_1$ spans the one-dimensional $K$-space $L_\eta$, while $B$ has no generic component, so both subsheaves have stalk $L_\eta$. Equality can be checked on stalks (a section belongs to either subsheaf exactly when it does locally), giving $A_U=L\otimes\mathcal O_C(-B)$, which is locally free of rank one. By definition of image, evaluation onto $A_U$ is surjective, so $U$ generates it. Each $s_i$ factors through $A_U$; the map $U\to H^0(C,A_U)$ is injective since its composite into $H^0(C,L)$ is the original inclusion.

source.place: Tag 0BE9 (lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective), local divisor-module description; elementary minimum-order ideal calculation and equality on stalks

proof.text: Write $A=A_U$. With respect to the local generator $t^{b_P}e$ of $A_P$, the order of $s_1$ is $\operatorname{ord}_{P,L}(s_1)-b_P$. Thus $E=\operatorname{div}_A(s_1)=D_1-B$ is effective. The rational-section isomorphism [lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section], applied to $L$ and to $A$, gives $L\simeq\mathcal O_C(D_1)$ and $A\simeq\mathcal O_C(E)$. The displayed isomorphisms induce isomorphisms on cohomology, hence preserve the Euler-characteristic degree of [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Both divisors are effective, so [lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc] identifies these degrees with their divisor degrees. By the definition in [def-sc-divisor], these are the sums of their coefficients. Consequently $a=\deg E\geq0$ and $d-a=\deg D_1-\deg E=\sum_P b_P\geq0$. This also identifies the divisor degree of $A$ used by Riemann--Roch below with its stated degree $a$.

source.place: Tag 0AYY (lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor), together with the rational-section divisor identification; nonnegative sums

proof.text:
Put $\omega=\Omega^1_{C/k}$. Since $C$ is smooth and integral of dimension one, its single fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is equidimensional of dimension one; thus its relative dimension is one in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] to see that $\omega$ is invertible. Set $N=\omega\otimes A^{-1}$: on a trivializing open, the dual of a generator of $A$ generates $A^{-1}$, so $N$ is invertible and evaluation identifies $A\otimes N$ with $\omega$. Apply [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] to $\mathcal O_C$ and to $A$. All the section spaces used here are finite-dimensional, $h^0(C,\omega)=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=g$, and $h^0(C,N)=h^1(C,A)$. Put $n=h^0(C,A)$ and $h=h^1(C,A)$. Higher cohomology vanishes by the same cited theorem, and [lem-sc-riemann-roch], with the degree identification from step 3, gives
$$n-h=a+1-g.$$
The injection of step 2 now yields $q\leq n$, and $n>0$.

source.place: Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), 0BS6 (lemma-rr): Serre duality, finite dimensionality, higher vanishing and Riemann--Roch on a smooth proper curve

proof.text: Suppose $h>0$. By [lem-pc-rational-points-dense], the nonempty smooth $C$ has a $k$-rational point $P$; In every affine neighbourhood of $P$, evaluation to $k$ contains every constant, hence is surjective and has maximal kernel, so $P$ is closed there and has residue field $k$. Any specialization of $P$ has an affine neighbourhood containing $P$, and therefore equals $P$. Thus $P$ is closed in $C$. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], $R=\mathcal O_{C,P}\subset K$ is a DVR with fraction field $K$, and $k\to R/\mathfrak m$ is an isomorphism. Choose $K$-bases $e$ of $A_\eta$ and $f$ of $N_\eta$; their product is a basis of $\omega_\eta$ under $A\otimes N\simeq\omega$. By [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk], generic germs in these bases identify $H^0(C,A)$ and $H^0(C,N)$ with subspaces $V,W\subset K$ of dimensions $n,h$. Products of global sections of $A$ and $N$ are global sections of $\omega$, and their generic coefficients in the basis $ef$ are exactly $vw$; this follows by multiplying the local coefficients in line-bundle trivializations. The same injectivity for $\omega$ puts the span of these products in an ambient subspace of $K$ of dimension $g$. Apply [lem-sfb-residue-valuation-product-dimension] to $R,K,V,W$ to obtain $n+h-1\leq g$. Combining with step 4, $h=n-a-1+g$, gives $2n\leq a+2$, hence $n\leq a/2+1$.

source.place: Section 2.4, Theorem 5, printed p.10 and Figure 1: agent reconstruction of the Clifford bound via multiplication of complementary sections and the rational-residue product lemma

proof.text: If $h=0$, step 4 gives $n=a+1-g$, so $n\leq\max\{a+1-g,a/2+1\}$. If $h>0$, step 5 gives $n\leq a/2+1$, hence the same maximum bound. Together with $q\leq n$ from step 4 and $0\leq a\leq d$ from step 3, this proves all the inequalities. These inequalities are read in $\mathbf R$, using the usual inclusions of the integer degrees and dimensions.

source.place: Section 2.4, Theorem 5, printed p.10 and Figure 1: the nonspecial Riemann--Roch line and the special Clifford line

proof.text: If $q=1$, write $U=k s$ with $s\ne0$. The map $\mathcal O_C\to L$, $1\mapsto s$, is injective: in each local trivialization its coefficient is nonzero in a domain, as follows from the injective generic-germ map in [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk]. Its image is precisely $A_U$, so it induces $\mathcal O_C\simeq A_U$. By [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], $a=\chi(\mathcal O_C)-\chi(\mathcal O_C)=0$. If $U=H^0(C,L)$ and evaluation is surjective, its image is $L$ by definition, so $A_U=L$ as submodules and $a=d$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NZ-e4112a8ee (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Fifth delivery of the same split. The four earlier heads (1d7f, 4d5c, 852a, ec38) all passed on the mathematics; each landing was refused only because the side completion was not promoted. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit with an empty proof, and the new node is absent from both, so this delivery is not superseded. There is no repair note for the item. The item's statement, stmt_deps, source, unit, created and from fields are identical to the live node's. The only change from ec38 is one sentence in step 2: at the generic point, the nonzero germ of s_1 spans the one-dimensional L_eta and B has no generic component, so A_U and L⊗O(-B) agree there too. This is correct and uses the generic-stalk lemma that step 1 already cites. There is one cosmetic typo ('closed points, At'). The new node is byte-identical to ec38. I re-read all 16 cited statements in this snapshot and re-checked every step. (1) The common divisor B satisfies 0<=B<=D_1, using generic-stalk (2)/(3) and the finite support of rational-section divisors. (2) The stalks of the image are t^{b_P}O_P, which equals O(-B)_P by divisor-module-local with n_P=-b_P. (3) E=D_1-B is effective, and degree-agrees-sc is applied only to the effective D_1 and E, giving 0<=a<=d and the degree that RR needs. (4) Serre duality for O and for A gives h^0(omega)=g and h^1(A)=h^0(N); RR(1) then gives n-h=a+1-g. (5) A rational point exists and is closed with residue field k; generic germs and products into H^0(omega) plus the new lemma give n+h-1<=g, hence 2n<=a+2. (6),(7) Case split and the edge clauses are correct. The new valuation product-dimension lemma is true by a leading-term staircase argument; ⟨1,t⟩^2 attains the bound, and the residue hypothesis is necessary (counterexample k=R, R=C[t]_(t)). It is self-contained and is not a duplicate or a restatement of a clause of the item. Batch-5 flag: degree-agrees-sc, Serre duality and RR reach def-trf-schematically-dense-open only through coherent-hi, Chow's lemma and Nagata. That endpoint is a general definition, and none of these results is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so I accept the citations. The 14 generic curve/coherent tool_uses are accepted. No SGA source is cited. No changes. Maintainer note: L should promote and land this rather than re-dispatch it.
